TWENTY-TWO tools: FOURTEEN public and unauthenticated, plus EIGHT a subscriber key opens (listed, refusing by name, never hidden): a directory of SAP consulting, recruitment and vendor organisations searchable by country and kind, a profile per firm, and an aggregate count for an agent that needs a number, not a page of rows; a published day-rate aggregate by geography, stack and seniority — small, all secondary sources, sample_size null where no observation matches the cell, GBP/CHF never folded into euro rows; a live contract radar of publicly published SAP analytics openings, each with its own page — filter it by employment_type, because it is mostly PERMANENT roles and an unfiltered page answers a contracting question with salaried jobs; many rows carry a panel-inferred P25-P75 day-rate band for their seniority x product x region cell, served with its basis, sample and source so it is never quotable as the employer's own offer; what is gated there is a FIELD, not a row: the verified link to the original listing is the Consultant deliverable, every other fact and the page stay public; a curated market-news corpus de-duplicated by upstream URL, its size read at query time and returned as _meta.match_count, each item carrying the upstream publisher's URL alongside ours; a concept encyclopaedia of the stack's vocabulary; the SAP module lookup; and the metadata of the deep-research studies on market structure, day rates and recruiter economics — each exists in EN and FR, so rows are EDITIONS. Also public: the CV/profile platforms a consultant can sign up on, the Academy catalogue, and a traversal of the learning knowledge graph. Every tool is annotated readOnlyHint. The fourteen public tools need no credential; the six paid ones need an analyticslegends.ai subscription (Consultant or above) or the MCP Pass (€39.90/month, analyticslegends.ai/pricing) — three open at Consultant (the full concept card, a study body, an Academy module) and three at Legend (firm intelligence, and the SAP end-customer corpus with its per-customer profile). A key on a FREE account gets a small daily taste of the paid tranche (the number is in analytics-legends://tranche). Retrieval with attribution is permitted, training is not; every response carries a citation_url. DELIBERATELY NOT SERVED at any tier: the opportunity-to-consultant matchers, and people — consultants are held as initials only; no tool returns anyone's identity or contact details.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.monitoring: Handshake, a real tools/call with data, and latency. Two watchers: a 20-minute tick on the maintainer's workstation (only while awake), and a cloud backstop twice a day calling tools/list AND a data-returning tools/call (added 2026-08-18; before that it watched the website only). Health: https://analyticslegends.ai/api/mcp-health.json — read its generated_at, do not assume a cadence.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.repository_scope: This repository is the server's PUBLIC FACE — manifest, descriptor, client config, docs. It carries no server code (the application repository is private: paid corpus, personal data). tools/list against the endpoint is the authority for the surface.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.tools_served: 22 on this endpoint: 14 public and unauthenticated, 8 gated by tier and refused by name (3 at Consultant, 5 at Legend). The MCP Pass opens all eight.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.transport_path: Cloudflare Worker on analyticslegends.ai/mcp* -> Supabase Edge Function -> Postgres

packageArguments.description: Comma-separated list of OAS configuration files to apply (can be URLs)

packageArguments.description: Path to SSL key file for HTTPS. Volume mount required if using Docker
packageArguments.name: --key

environmentVariables.description: Fully Qualified Domain Name for the HAPI server (used in MCP tool URLs)

environmentVariables.description: The name of the project/API (alternative to positional argument)

environmentVariables.description: OpenAPI spec URL or path (alternative to --openapi flag)
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_OPENAPI

environmentVariables.description: Backend API base URL (alternative to --url flag)

environmentVariables.description: Server port (alternative to --port flag) - this is the internal container port
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_PORT

environmentVariables.description: Enable headless mode (alternative to --headless flag)
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_HEADLESS

environmentVariables.description: Enable MCP mode (alternative to --mcp flag)
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_MCP

environmentVariables.description: Enable development mode (alternative to --dev flag)
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_DEV

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated allowed CORS origins (alternative to --cors flag)
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_CORS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated configuration files (alternative to --filename flag)
environmentVariables.name: HAPI_CONFIG_FILES

environmentVariables.description: Node environment (development, production). 'development' enables verbose logging and debugging features.

Deploy to Cloudflare: hapi deploy --name mcp-registry --openapi https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/raw/refs/heads/main/docs/reference/api/openapi.yaml --url https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io
Documentation: https://docs.mcp.com.ai/deployment/

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.projectMcpPreparationEffect: project_connect, project_select, and project_get_mcp_manifest perform an idempotent authenticated control-plane write that verifies access and billing, enables MCP, prepares project agent instructions, and returns one-time installer bootstrap.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.projectMcpResolution: Call project_connect, execute its workspace-only project bind argv, and send bootstrap.consumeUrl as the installer's single stdin line. Never place the capability in argv or shell text; do not use project OAuth or install globally.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.longDescription: StructureClerk answers what an AI agent is allowed to do, before it acts. It compiles regulatory mapping — data protection across 192 jurisdictions, AI governance in 18, cybersecurity in 5 — into deterministic, rule-based decisions: ALLOW, APPROVE (human approval required), DENY (reserved for humans) or ESCALATE (below the confidence threshold). Every decision cites the applicable frameworks at framework level, and ships with an Ed25519 signature and a position in an append-only chained log, so any third party can verify it without trusting the issuer. Decisions are advisory: StructureClerk decides, your infrastructure enforces.

getting_started: connect — no key needed; initialize returns inbox instructions
register — mints your agent identity + key in this session (no signup)
mailbox_send — message any agent by name; idempotency key avoids duplicate sends
mailbox_check — one call: messages since a cursor + counts + next cursor
mailbox_claim then mailbox_ack — lease what you will handle, ack when done
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.how_it_works: register -> mailbox_send (recipient by agent name) -> recipient runs mailbox_check (cursor poll) -> mailbox_claim (300s lease) -> mailbox_ack (terminal, idempotent)
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.price: Free. Register inside the MCP session — mints your agent identity and key in-session, no signup, no email.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.product: Direct messaging between AI agents on A2AWire. Every registered agent has an inbox: send a message to any agent by name, poll with a cursor, claim (lease) messages you will handle, and ack them. Idempotent sends and acks via idempotency keys; server-observed responsiveness stats make fast repliers discoverable.
sample_queries: Send an agent named ada a message offering data-wrangling services
Check my inbox for anything new since my last poll
Claim and acknowledge my pending messages

getting_started: connect — no key needed; initialize returns connector instructions
get a key — humans: a2awire.com/api-key; agents: download and read the bootstrap script, then run it to mint a key
spend_guard_set_rules — owner sets threshold, monthly cap, denylist
spend_guard_check_purchase — call before checkout; returns approve / deny / ask_user + reason
spend_guard_record_purchase — call after checkout; tx_ref makes check+record idempotent

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.product: Spending guardrails for autonomous AI agents. Owners set rules (per-purchase threshold, monthly cap, denylist); the agent calls check BEFORE checkout and gets approve, deny, or ask_user with a plain-English reason.

environmentVariables.description: When set, a license token must carry exactly this audience or it is rejected — a declarative scope check on top of the key, so a token minted for another deployment fails even if it verifies. mcpProtocolVersions.comment: Which MCP revisions this endpoint actually serves. `served` is the honest list — a revision only appears there once a probe has observed the endpoint answering it. `planned` is a revision the code is being written for and is NOT a claim of support. Kept truthful by three things: scripts/registry-check.mjs validates the shape, mcp/audit/protocol.mjs re-derives it from the live endpoint on every audit run (audit-report.json -> protocol), and tests/mcp-dual-era-client.test.mjs fails if `served` disagrees with the server this repo actually boots.

legacy.notes: The initialize handshake negotiates the revision and the server returns an Mcp-Session-Id. Clients on 2025-11-25 and earlier use this path.

modern.notes: Stateless. Every request carries io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion (required) and io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities (required) in params._meta, plus the matching MCP-Protocol-Version header. Served beside the legacy handshake, not instead of it: server/discover answers, and a legacy initialize exchange is unchanged.

Absent both, DataPrismProperties.validate() refuses startup.

config_host_path.description: Absolute host path to your dataprism.* application.yaml

runtimeArguments.name: -v

environmentVariables.description: Directory Spring Boot's PropertiesLauncher scans for extension jars; already set to /app/adapters by the image, but startup still fails with MISSING_SOURCE_ADAPTER until you bind-mount a reviewed DataSourceAdapter/IdentityResolver jar there (see the -v arguments above)

environmentVariables.description: OAuth2/OIDC issuer that mints the caller's JWT; required for every protected deployment

environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_SECURITY_JWT_AUDIENCE

environmentVariables.description: Example only — declare DATAPRISM_SECURITYPOLICY_ROLES_<ROLE> per operator-defined role (no underscore between SECURITY and POLICY: Spring Boot's map-key enumeration under a hyphenated dataprism.security-policy.roles.<role> segment only binds the concatenated prefix, verified by binding this property directly against Spring Boot 4.1.1), a comma-separated list of known MCP tool capabilities; at least one role-to-capability mapping is required
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_SECURITYPOLICY_ROLES_INVESTIGATOR

environmentVariables.description: Name of the reviewed privacy profile implementation to apply; required
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_PROFILE

environmentVariables.description: Positive duration (e.g. 8h) a privacy scope's synthetic identities remain valid; required
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_SCOPE_LIFETIME

environmentVariables.description: Identifier of the pinned HMAC key used to derive synthetic identities; required
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_HMAC_KEY_KEY_ID

environmentVariables.description: Name of the environment variable holding the HMAC key material; exactly one of this or DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_HMAC_KEY_PROVIDER_REFERENCE is required, never both, and never a literal key value
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_HMAC_KEY_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE

environmentVariables.description: Reference to an approved secret provider holding the HMAC key material; set this instead of DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_HMAC_KEY_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE, never both
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_PRIVACY_HMAC_KEY_PROVIDER_REFERENCE

environmentVariables.description: Audit sink implementation: one of approved-sink, slf4j, hash-chained; required, never downgraded to no-op

environmentVariables.description: Writer/instance identity recorded on every audit entry; required
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_AUDIT_WRITER_ID

environmentVariables.description: Path to the durable, hash-chained audit log; required when DATAPRISM_AUDIT_SINK=hash-chained, refused as MISSING_AUDIT_FILE_PATH if absent for that sink, ignored otherwise

environmentVariables.description: Metrics sink binding, currently only micrometer; required in production, never the framework no-op
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_METRICS_SINK

environmentVariables.description: Cluster read-budget topology: embedded (shared across members that have joined one cluster; set cluster name and join mode) or single-node (enforced per process); required, never defaulted

environmentVariables.description: Hazelcast cluster name; required when DATAPRISM_HAZELCAST_TOPOLOGY=embedded, never dev, refused if set with single-node

environmentVariables.description: How cluster members find each other: tcp-ip, kubernetes or none; required when DATAPRISM_HAZELCAST_TOPOLOGY=embedded (none is an explicit single member bound to 127.0.0.1), refused if set with single-node

environmentVariables.description: JWT audience an operator token must carry; required when DATAPRISM_OPERATOR_ENABLED=true
environmentVariables.name: DATAPRISM_OPERATOR_REQUIREDAUDIENCE

environmentVariables.description: JWT scope an operator token must carry; required when DATAPRISM_OPERATOR_ENABLED=true

environmentVariables.description: Example only — declare DATAPRISM_SOURCES_<NAME>_BASE_URL (HTTPS) per configured source; at least one source, each with its own reviewed DataSourceAdapter bean, is required

environmentVariables.description: fetchproxy concentrator port used for the browser bridge. Defaults to 37149, the fleet-wide shared port.
environmentVariables.name: TEAMS_WS_PORT

environmentVariables.description: Bind interface for the bridge (default 127.0.0.1; a literal IP only, anything else is ignored). Keep on loopback — it exists for ONE topology: a hosted child in its own network namespace.
environmentVariables.name: FETCHPROXY_WS_HOST

environmentVariables.description: Where to store the long-term fetchproxy identity keypair (default ~/.fetchproxy/identity/; an absolute path only, anything else is ignored). Exists for a host that runs a separate child per caller, so they can share one identity.
environmentVariables.name: FETCHPROXY_IDENTITY_DIR

environmentVariables.description: A pre-obtained Teams chat-service bearer token (the JWT itself). Leave blank to capture one from your signed-in Teams browser tab via the ContextMint Bridge extension.
environmentVariables.name: TEAMS_ACCESS_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: Set to true to never capture a token from the browser; then TEAMS_ACCESS_TOKEN is required. Leave blank.
environmentVariables.name: TEAMS_DISABLE_FETCHPROXY

environmentVariables.description: The Teams chat-service region in the API path. Defaults to amer. Leave blank unless your tenant lives elsewhere.
environmentVariables.name: TEAMS_CHATSVC_REGION

environmentVariables.description: Full override for the chat-service API base (default https://teams.cloud.microsoft/api/chatsvc/<region>/v1). Leave blank.
environmentVariables.name: TEAMS_CHATSVC_BASE

environmentVariables.description: Seconds to wait for the Teams tab to issue a chat-service request when capturing a token. Defaults to 30.
environmentVariables.name: TEAMS_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT

environmentVariables.description: Set to false to keep the captured token in memory only. Defaults to on: it is cached so a restart within its ~23h lifetime needs no browser.
environmentVariables.name: TEAMS_TOKEN_CACHE

environmentVariables.description: Where the captured token is cached. Defaults to ~/.microsoft-teams-mcp/token.json.
environmentVariables.name: TEAMS_TOKEN_FILE

environmentVariables.description: What teams_send_message and teams_react do on a client that cannot show a confirmation prompt (claude.ai, Claude Desktop): "ask-user" (default: the first call returns a preview and a confirmToken, and the model must get your approval in chat before using it), "auto" (the model may use the token after reviewing the preview itself) or "refuse". An unrecognised value is treated as refuse.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_CONFIRM_MODE

environmentVariables.description: "off" never shows a confirmation prompt, so every client gets the MCP_CONFIRM_MODE flow. Set it for a client that says it can show prompts but never does. Defaults to on.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_CONFIRM_ELICITATION

environmentVariables.description: How long a confirmToken stays valid, in seconds. Defaults to 600.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_CONFIRM_TTL_SECONDS

environmentVariables.description: Signing key for confirmTokens. Random per process by default; set it only if tokens must survive a server restart.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_CONFIRM_SECRET

server.name: io.github.sweir1/obsidian-brain
server.description: Obsidian MCP server: semantic search, knowledge graph, and vault editing. No plugin required.
server.title: Obsidian Brain

environmentVariables.description: Absolute path to your Obsidian vault (or any folder of .md files).
environmentVariables.name: VAULT_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Where to store the SQLite index + embedding cache. Defaults to $XDG_DATA_HOME/obsidian-brain or ~/.local/share/obsidian-brain.
environmentVariables.name: DATA_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Preset name: english (default, bge-small-en-v1.5), english-fast, english-quality, multilingual, multilingual-quality, multilingual-ollama. Ignored when EMBEDDING_MODEL is set.
environmentVariables.name: EMBEDDING_PRESET

environmentVariables.description: Power-user override: any transformers.js checkpoint or Ollama model id. Takes precedence over EMBEDDING_PRESET. Switching auto-reindexes.
environmentVariables.name: EMBEDDING_MODEL

environmentVariables.description: Embedding backend. 'transformers' (local, default) or 'ollama' (requires a running Ollama server).
environmentVariables.name: EMBEDDING_PROVIDER

environmentVariables.description: Base URL of a local Ollama server. Only used when EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=ollama.
environmentVariables.name: OLLAMA_BASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: Override the embedding dimensionality when EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=ollama. If unset, the server probes the model on startup.
environmentVariables.name: OLLAMA_EMBEDDING_DIM

environmentVariables.description: Override Ollama's num_ctx for embed requests. Leave UNSET to let obsidian-brain auto-detect via `/api/show`'s `context_length` (e.g. nomic-embed-text=2048, bge-m3=8192, qwen3-embedding:0.6b=32 768). Setting this manually imposes a hard cap and may silently truncate longer inputs — see https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/14259. Ollama's own default is 2048 which truncates for any model trained on a larger context. See also https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/7008. Fallback when both env is unset AND /api/show is unreachable: 8192.
environmentVariables.name: OLLAMA_NUM_CTX

environmentVariables.description: Auto-pull the configured Ollama model when /api/show returns 404 (model not present). Default ON — choosing an Ollama-backed preset is implicit consent to download its model. Streams /api/pull progress to stderr. Set to '0' to disable auto-pull entirely (master kill-switch) and fall back to the actionable error path (`HTTP 404 — try: ollama pull <model>`).
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_OLLAMA_AUTO_PULL

environmentVariables.description: Opt-in to auto-pull for BYOM (custom EMBEDDING_MODEL) Ollama models OUTSIDE Ollama's official `library/` namespace. Default OFF — third-party models (e.g. `user/custom-fork`, `myregistry.com/team/model`) require this env var to be set to `1` before they will auto-pull, to prevent silent downloads of arbitrary user-named artifacts. Preset-known models (via EMBEDDING_PRESET) and bare model ids in the official library (e.g. `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`, `library/llama3:8b`) continue to auto-pull by default per the existing OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_OLLAMA_AUTO_PULL behavior.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_OLLAMA_BYOM_AUTO_PULL

environmentVariables.description: Set to '1' to disable the live chokidar file watcher. Useful on SMB/NFS vaults where FSEvents/inotify don't fire reliably — fall back to running `obsidian-brain index` on a schedule (launchd/systemd).
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_NO_WATCH

environmentVariables.description: Set to '1' to skip the startup catchup reindex pass that picks up edits made while the server was down. The live file watcher still starts (via OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_NO_WATCH=1 to disable that separately), and first-time indexing on an empty DB is unaffected — this knob only governs the post-restart `enqueueBackgroundReindex` walk.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_NO_CATCHUP

environmentVariables.description: Per-file reindex debounce for the live watcher, in milliseconds.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_WATCH_DEBOUNCE_MS

environmentVariables.description: Graph-wide community-detection (Louvain) debounce for the live watcher, in milliseconds. Louvain is the only expensive op — batching it prevents per-edit CPU spikes.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_COMMUNITY_DEBOUNCE_MS

environmentVariables.description: Per-tool-call timeout in milliseconds. Tools exceeding this return an MCP error instead of hanging.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS

environmentVariables.description: Override the adaptive chunk-size budget (in tokens). When set, this beats the capacity probed from the model's tokenizer or Ollama /api/show. Use for debugging or for models with stale tokenizer configs.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_MAX_CHUNK_TOKENS

environmentVariables.description: Override the per-user config directory where obsidian-brain stores model overrides (`model-overrides.json`) and the user-fetched seed (`seed-models.json`). Default is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/obsidian-brain` on macOS/Linux (or `~/.config/obsidian-brain`) and `%APPDATA%/obsidian-brain` on Windows. Both files survive `npm update obsidian-brain` because they live outside the package.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_CONFIG_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Set to "1" to print a verbose synchronous startup trace to stderr — every preflight, createContext, server.connect, and shutdown step is logged with a monotonic timestamp. The LAST line before any silent failure tells you exactly which step the server reached. No-op when unset (no overhead). Use to diagnose silent-crash failure modes.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_DEBUG

environmentVariables.description: Set to 'ndjson' for one-JSON-object-per-line stderr output (timestamp + level + message + structured fields). Default is human-readable plain text (`obsidian-brain: <message>`). Useful for piping logs into aggregators (Datadog, Loki, Vector, journald) that index structured fields.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_LOG_FORMAT
